description: Standalone catalogue of the voice-leading, interval-leading, SATB, counterpoint, spacing, doubling, cadence, harmony, and dissonance rules currently implemented or explicitly mentioned in Harm31a.

notes: The executable rule profiles live in src/domain/rules/ruleProfiles31.ts.
The JSON files in src/data/ruleProfiles are placeholders with empty enabledRuleIds and are not the active profile source.
The rule engine currently filters by enabledRuleIds and applies severityOverrides. Other profile fields are consumed by rules or harmoniser code only where noted below.

basicIntervalClassifier.0: unison, or octave when absolute motion is nonzero and 0 mod 31

profiles.name: Strict counterpoint
profiles.description: Strictest first-pass profile for species-like voice-leading and dissonance treatment.

profiles.name: Common-practice SATB
profiles.description: Balanced 18th/19th-century SATB profile for harmony exercises.

profiles.name: Nineteenth-century expanded
profiles.description: More permissive profile for later common-practice color and freer doubling.

profiles.name: Custom revisionist 31
profiles.description: Experimental native-31 profile with softer historical constraints.

implementationNotes: All implemented rule diagnostics operate on Score31 notes through absoluteStep31 and native 31-EDO pitch-class distances.

All four executable profiles currently enable the same CORE_RULE_IDS31; profiles differ through severityOverrides, allowed dissonance labels, beamWidth, chord vocabulary, hiddenPerfectStrictness metadata, and spacing thresholds.

hiddenPerfectStrictness is declared in profiles, but the current evaluator does not branch on this field. Hidden perfect rules remain enabled wherever their rule IDs are enabled, with only severityOverrides changing output severity.
allowedDissonanceTypes is declared in profiles and used as profile metadata, but the current non-chord-tone rule is heuristic and does not yet classify individual dissonance types.
upperVoiceWarningMax is declared in spacingThresholds31 but the current spacing rule reads sopranoAltoMax, altoTenorMax, and tenorBassMax directly.

The harmoniser uses final rule diagnostics for hard errors and also applies search-time costs and prefilters for range, SATB ordering, severe spacing, smoothness, root doubling, and parallel perfect intervals.

implementedRules.name: SATB voice ranges
implementedRules.definition: Every sounding note must stay within the configured range for its SATB voice.
implementedRules.trigger: A note's absoluteStep31 is lower than the active voice range low step or higher than the active voice range high step.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Move the note into the voice range or choose a different voice/register.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Candidate voicing generation only creates notes inside src/data/voiceRanges.json ranges; final diagnostics also reject out-of-range notes as hard errors.

implementedRules.name: Upper-voice spacing
implementedRules.definition: Adjacent upper voices should not exceed the profile's configured maximum spacing.
implementedRules.trigger: The S-A span or A-T span, measured as upper absoluteStep31 minus lower absoluteStep31, is greater than the profile threshold.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Bring the upper voices closer together or redistribute the chord tones.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Candidate voicings with S-A or A-T spacing above 31 steps are rejected before search; smaller spacing discomfort adds cost above 18 steps.

implementedRules.name: Tenor-bass spacing
implementedRules.definition: Tenor and bass may be wider than the upper voices, but a very wide T-B span is flagged as stylistic risk.
implementedRules.trigger: The T-B span, measured as tenor absoluteStep31 minus bass absoluteStep31, is greater than the profile threshold.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Consider a closer tenor position unless this is a deliberate open voicing.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Candidate voicings with T-B spacing above 48 steps are rejected before search; smaller T-B spacing discomfort adds cost above 31 steps.

implementedRules.name: No voice crossing
implementedRules.definition: SATB vertical order should keep soprano above alto, alto above tenor, and tenor above bass.
implementedRules.trigger: For any adjacent SATB pair, the upper voice absoluteStep31 is lower than the lower voice absoluteStep31.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Move one of the voices back into normal vertical order.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Candidate voicings are rejected unless S >= A >= T >= B in absoluteStep31; final diagnostics treat crossings as hard errors.

implementedRules.name: No voice overlap
implementedRules.definition: An adjacent voice should not move beyond the previous register of its neighbor between two sonorities.
implementedRules.trigger: For adjacent voices, upperTo is below lowerFrom, or lowerTo is above upperFrom.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Use smaller motion or revoice the destination chord.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics score overlaps as warnings; overlap cost is included through diagnosticCost when ranking generated solutions.

implementedRules.name: No parallel unisons
implementedRules.definition: Two voices should not move in the same nonzero direction from one exact unison to another exact unison.
implementedRules.trigger: Any ordered voice pair has nonzero same-direction motion and the previous and current vertical intervals both classify as unison.
implementedRules.perfectIntervalDefinition31: Unison is pitch-class distance 0 with absolute vertical interval 0.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Use contrary or oblique motion, or change one chord tone.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics treat parallel unisons as hard errors; search-time parallel perfect penalty also catches same-kind perfect intervals.

implementedRules.name: No parallel perfect fifths
implementedRules.definition: Two voices should not move in the same nonzero direction from one perfect fifth to another perfect fifth.
implementedRules.trigger: Any ordered voice pair has nonzero same-direction motion and the previous and current vertical intervals both classify as fifth.
implementedRules.perfectIntervalDefinition31: Perfect fifth is native 31-EDO pitch-class distance 18.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Use contrary or oblique motion, or change one chord tone.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: The harmoniser adds a 1200 search penalty for parallel perfect intervals and final diagnostics treat parallel fifths as hard errors.

implementedRules.name: No parallel octaves
implementedRules.definition: Two voices should not move in the same nonzero direction from one octave to another octave.
implementedRules.trigger: Any ordered voice pair has nonzero same-direction motion and the previous and current vertical intervals both classify as octave.
implementedRules.perfectIntervalDefinition31: Octave is native 31-EDO pitch-class distance 0 with nonzero absolute vertical interval.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Use contrary or oblique motion, or change one chord tone.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: The harmoniser adds a 1200 search penalty for parallel perfect intervals and final diagnostics treat parallel octaves as hard errors.

implementedRules.name: Hidden/direct fifths in outer voices
implementedRules.definition: The outer voices should not approach a perfect fifth by similar motion when the soprano leaps.
implementedRules.trigger: Soprano and bass both move in the same nonzero direction, soprano motion is greater than 5 native steps, and the destination S-B interval classifies as a perfect fifth.
implementedRules.perfectIntervalDefinition31: Perfect fifth is native 31-EDO pitch-class distance 18.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Approach the perfect interval by contrary motion or stepwise soprano motion.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics score hidden/direct fifths as warnings or style notices depending on profile.

implementedRules.name: Hidden/direct octaves in outer voices
implementedRules.definition: The outer voices should not approach an octave by similar motion when the soprano leaps.
implementedRules.trigger: Soprano and bass both move in the same nonzero direction, soprano motion is greater than 5 native steps, and the destination S-B interval classifies as an octave.
implementedRules.perfectIntervalDefinition31: Octave is native 31-EDO pitch-class distance 0 with nonzero absolute vertical interval.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Approach the perfect interval by contrary motion or stepwise soprano motion.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics score hidden/direct octaves as warnings or style notices depending on profile.

implementedRules.name: Large melodic leap
implementedRules.definition: A single voice should avoid very large melodic leaps unless justified and compensated.
implementedRules.trigger: Any voice moves by more than 18 native 31-EDO steps between adjacent slices.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Prefer stepwise motion or compensate the leap in the opposite direction.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add cost for large leaps; search-time smoothness cost also penalizes large motion in every voice.

implementedRules.name: Augmented melodic interval
implementedRules.definition: Altered or augmented melodic intervals are stylistically flagged for review.
implementedRules.trigger: Any voice moves by at least 6 native steps and classifyBasicInterval31 returns unclassified.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Check whether the altered spelling and resolution are intentional.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add a style cost when this rule fires.

implementedRules.name: Leap compensation
implementedRules.definition: A large leap is usually followed by motion in the opposite direction.
implementedRules.trigger: A voice makes a previous motion greater than 18 native steps, then continues in the same nonzero direction on the next motion.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Move the following note back by step if possible.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add a style cost when this rule fires.

implementedRules.name: Repeated-note stagnation
implementedRules.definition: Long repeated-note runs can make a line feel static.
implementedRules.trigger: A voice reaches four consecutive sounding notes with the same absoluteStep31.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Consider stepwise motion or a neighboring figure.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add a style cost when this rule fires.

implementedRules.name: Triad classification
implementedRules.definition: Classify stable three-or-more-note sonorities as native 31-EDO triads when confidence is high enough.
implementedRules.trigger: A vertical slice has at least three sounding notes and classifySonority31 returns a chord with confidence at least 0.65.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Use this as harmonic context for spacing, doubling, and dissonance checks.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Candidate chords use the profile's permittedChordVocabulary; final diagnostics can classify resulting sonorities.

implementedRules.name: Incomplete chord
implementedRules.definition: Flag a classified chord that appears to omit one or more expected chord tones.
implementedRules.trigger: A vertical slice has at least three sounding notes, classifySonority31 returns a chord, and missingSteps31 is nonempty.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Check whether the omission is intended or caused by doubling.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add a style cost for incomplete sonorities.

implementedRules.name: Doubled tendency tone
implementedRules.definition: Likely tendency pitch classes should normally not be doubled.
implementedRules.trigger: A vertical sonority doubles native pitch-class step 12, 17, 27, or 30.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Prefer doubling the root or a stable chord tone unless the tendency tone treatment is deliberate.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add warning or style cost; candidate voicing generation separately gives a small cost when the root is not doubled.

implementedRules.name: Basic cadence detection
implementedRules.definition: Identify a final outer-voice sonority that is stable enough to be a basic cadence candidate.
implementedRules.trigger: The last slice and previous slice exist, the last bass and soprano sound, and the final soprano-bass pitch-class distance is 0, 10, or 18.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: A future key-aware cadence pass can refine this label.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Generated solutions receive a small cadence score bonus when the final S-B pitch-class distance is 0, 10, or 18.
limitations: Not phrase-aware beyond checking the final slice

implementedRules.name: Non-chord tone candidate
implementedRules.definition: Flag a note that does not belong to the best first-pass chord classification for a four-or-more-note sonority.
implementedRules.trigger: A vertical slice has at least four sounding notes, classifySonority31 returns a chord, and nonChordNotes is nonempty.
implementedRules.diagnosticSuggestion: Check whether it behaves as a passing tone, neighbor tone, suspension, or appoggiatura.
implementedRules.harmoniserUse: Final diagnostics add error, warning, or style cost depending on profile.
limitations: Does not yet classify preparation, accent, duration, or resolution
Does not yet consume allowedDissonanceTypes to permit or reject a specific dissonance type

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Suspension preparation and resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: A suspension should be prepared as a consonance or retained tone, form a dissonance, and resolve according to its contrapuntal context.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: src/domain/rules/standardRules31.ts exports suspensionRules as an empty array.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Retardation resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: A retardation should be analyzed through preparation, dissonant delay, and resolution in the affected voice.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Passing tone treatment
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: A passing tone should be understood as linear stepwise motion between chord tones, with accent and duration affecting severity.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: Non-chord-tone candidates may suggest passing-tone interpretation, but no dedicated passing-tone classifier exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Neighbor tone treatment
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: A neighbor tone should leave and return to a stable pitch by local stepwise motion, with altered-neighbor variants allowed in expanded profiles.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Accented passing tone treatment
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: An accented passing tone should be judged by metrical accent, linear motion, and resolution.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: No metrical accent dissonance classifier exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Altered neighbor treatment
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: An altered neighbor should preserve spelling-sensitive 31-EDO identity and resolve intentionally.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Appoggiatura resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: An appoggiatura should be treated as an accented dissonance resolving by step, not as an autonomous chord by default.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Accented dissonance treatment
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Accented dissonances should be evaluated by accent, duration, preparation, and resolution.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Seventh preparation and resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: A seventh should be checked as a prepared or accented dissonance requiring contextual resolution unless the style supports another treatment.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: No dedicated seventh preparation/resolution evaluator exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Augmented sixth contrary-motion resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: An expanded sixth sonority often resolves by contrary motion and must preserve exact spelling and resolution evidence.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: No dedicated augmented-sixth detection or resolution evaluator exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Common-tone continuity
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Retained tones should be tracked through chromatic displacement, registral emphasis, or tonal redirection.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: No dedicated common-tone continuity evaluator exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Enharmonic reinterpretation and spelling-sensitive resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Changed spelling or resolution should be tracked without collapsing enharmonic spellings into an equal-tempered pitch-class set.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: The pitch model preserves spelling, but no dedicated enharmonic reinterpretation rule exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Linear chromaticism and altered-note resolution
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Altered notes should be checked for spelling, source notation, tendency, and resolution in the affected voice.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: The melodic.augmented rule flags altered or unclassified intervals, but no full linear-chromaticism evaluator exists.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Contrary-motion structures
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Contrary motion should be recognized as a preferred approach to some perfect intervals and expanded-sixth resolutions.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: Contrary motion is only indirectly favored because parallel-perfect and hidden-perfect rules require same or similar motion to trigger.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Cadential voice-leading confirmation
mentionedAs: expanded cadence suspensions and bass prolongation
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Cadences should be evaluated by bass motion, upper-voice resolution, phrase context, expected and actual resolution, and possible evasion or weakening.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: cadence.basic only checks final outer-voice stability by pitch-class distance 0, 10, or 18 and is not key-aware.

mentionedOrDeferredRules.name: Voice-leading-derived harmony before root-based labels
mentionedOrDeferredRules.expectedRuleIdea: Many verticalities should be explained as the result of simultaneous linear motions before assigning autonomous chord identity.
mentionedOrDeferredRules.currentImplementation: harmony.triad and dissonance.non-chord-tone are first-pass heuristics; no full linear-chord evaluator exists.

hardConstraintsMentionedInDocs: parallel unison/fifth/octave after final rule evaluation

searchTimeCosts.rootDoublingCost: 0 if root is doubled or present at least once in generated voicing; 6 otherwise
searchTimeCosts.cadenceBonus: 8 when final S-B pitch-class distance is 0, 10, or 18

candidatePrefilters: Generated notes are drawn from each voice range.
Voicings must satisfy S >= A >= T >= B.
Voicings are rejected when S-A > 31, A-T > 31, or T-B > 48 native steps.

currentLimitations: The rule checker is a rigorous first pass, not a complete historical treatise implementation.
Cadence detection is not key-aware or phrase-aware beyond the final sonority.

Suspension, retardation, passing-tone, neighbor-tone, appoggiatura, seventh-resolution, augmented-sixth, common-tone, and enharmonic-reinterpretation rules are mentioned or scaffolded but not fully implemented.
Later 19th-century licenses are currently represented mostly through profile severity changes and chord vocabulary, not detailed repertoire-specific exception logic.
The harmoniser is currently triad-focused and best suited to short examples.

catalogScope.exactPhraseNote: The exact phrase interval-leading is not used as a source-code rule category; this file treats interval-leading as rules whose trigger depends on melodic interval size, vertical interval class, interval approach, or intervallic cadence/key relation evidence.

contextConstruction: createTimeline31(score) builds vertical slices from note onsets.
Each enabled rule evaluates the shared RuleContext and returns diagnostics.
Profile severityOverrides are applied after diagnostics are created.

diagnosticShape.category: range | spacing | voice-leading | counterpoint | harmony | cadence | dissonance | doubling | notation

basicIntervalClassifier.0: unison, or octave when absolute motion is nonzero and 0 mod 31

definitions.unison: pitch-class distance 0 and absolute vertical interval 0
definitions.octave: pitch-class distance 0 and nonzero absolute vertical interval

implementedIntervalDrivenRules.consumedByHarmoniser: getParallelPerfectPenalty31 adds 1200 when a same-kind perfect interval is reached by same-direction nonzero motion.

definitions.0: unison, or octave when absolute motion is nonzero and 0 mod 31

additionalReturnValues.octave: absolute motion is nonzero and 0 mod 31
additionalReturnValues.compound: absolute motion is greater than 31 and not octave-equivalent
additionalReturnValues.unclassified: any other native 31-EDO interval not in the basic first-pass set

implementedIntervalDrivenRules.trigger: Any ordered SATB voice pair moves by nonzero same-direction motion from one same-kind perfect vertical interval to another.
Soprano and bass move by nonzero similar motion into a perfect fifth or octave while the soprano moves by more than 5 native steps.
A melodic motion larger than 18 native steps is flagged, and a following same-direction continuation is flagged as uncompensated.
The final soprano-bass pitch-class distance is 0, 10, or 18 after at least two slices exist.

mentionedIntervalDrivenRules.intervalBasis: expanded sixth resolving by contrary motion
seventh above bass or root treated as prepared or accented dissonance requiring contextual resolution
relative, fifth, mediant, chromatic-mediant, submediant, and tonal-return relations are mentioned as intervallic research categories, not executable app rules.

mentionedRelations.intervallicRelation: major or minor sixth or inverse third

rules.expectedRuleIdea: Retained tones should be tracked through chromatic displacement, registral emphasis, or tonal redirection.
rules.currentImplementation: No dedicated common-tone continuity evaluator exists.

rules.name: Enharmonic reinterpretation and spelling-sensitive resolution
rules.expectedRuleIdea: Changed spelling or resolution should be tracked without collapsing enharmonic spellings into an equal-tempered pitch-class set.
rules.currentImplementation: The pitch model preserves spelling, but no dedicated enharmonic reinterpretation rule exists.

rules.name: Linear chromaticism and altered-note resolution
rules.expectedRuleIdea: Altered notes should be checked for spelling, source notation, tendency, and resolution in the affected voice.
rules.currentImplementation: The melodic.augmented rule flags altered or unclassified intervals, but no full linear-chromaticism evaluator exists.

rules.name: Contrary-motion structures
rules.expectedRuleIdea: Contrary motion should be recognized as a preferred approach to some perfect intervals and expanded-sixth resolutions.
rules.currentImplementation: Contrary motion is only indirectly favored because parallel-perfect and hidden-perfect rules require same or similar motion to trigger.

rules.name: Cadential voice-leading confirmation
mentionedAs: expanded cadence suspensions and bass prolongation
rules.expectedRuleIdea: Cadences should be evaluated by bass motion, upper-voice resolution, phrase context, expected and actual resolution, and possible evasion or weakening.
rules.currentImplementation: cadence.basic only checks final outer-voice stability by pitch-class distance 0, 10, or 18 and is not key-aware.

rules.name: Voice-leading-derived harmony before root-based labels
rules.expectedRuleIdea: Many verticalities should be explained as the result of simultaneous linear motions before assigning autonomous chord identity.
rules.currentImplementation: harmony.triad and dissonance.non-chord-tone are first-pass heuristics; no full linear-chord evaluator exists.
